stories.title: US attacks Iran for ninth day as shipping concerns grow
stories.summary: US forces hit Iran for a ninth consecutive day as concerns grow over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran said two oil tankers had exploded and been immobilised. In a statement, US Central Command said it had begun "a new wave of strikes" aimed at "degrading" Iran's ability to attack commercial vessels in the strait's vital shipping lanes. It gave no further details. The strikes are part of an escalating cycle of attacks between the US and Iran after an interim ceasefire agreement signed a month ago unravelled, deepening a struggle for control over the Strait of Hormuz that has disrupted energy supplies and stoked fears of global inflation. Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, citing its own reporters, said US missiles struck several Iranian cities early this morning.

stories.title: Man charged over incident where car driven at group
stories.summary: A man in his 20s has been charged in relation to an incident in Skerries, Co Dublin where a car was driven at a number of people. Gardaí said they responded to reports of a public order incident at Harbour Road at around 9.30pm on Saturday night, when a large number of youths gathered and a fight broke out. During the course of the incident, a car was driven at a number of people. Three teenagers - two girls and a boy - were taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Another male was also reported to have received non-life-threatening injuries.

stories.title: Burnham to promise cost-of-living relief in PM speech
stories.summary: Andy Burnham will enter 10 Downing Street as the UK's new prime minister, promising to give people "breathing room" against the rising cost of living. In his first speech as PM, Mr Burnham will urge the country to be honest about the challenges it faces and call for "reflection and resolution". He will also say he is "acutely conscious" that the UK has had seven prime ministers in the last decade, stressing the need for more stable and responsible politics and pledging to restore faith in government. Allies of Mr Burnham said he will argue that political stability must deliver "tangible" improvements along with the "breathing room" on the cost of living that he has previously promised.

stories.title: Torres: 'Destiny was written' for Spain to triumph
stories.summary: Spain forward Ferran Torres said "destiny was written" after firing his country to World Cup glory against Argentina. Substitute Torres struck in the 106th minute to earn a 1-0 extra-time win over the defending champions in New Jersey. "I think in the end the goal came from 47 million people (approximately the population of Spain), not just those of us that are here," he said, speaking to FIFA host broadcasters in the mixed zone after the match. "Today destiny was written, it was made for us to win. We're far from our people today but we tried to be as close as possible to them.

stories.title: Britain's new Prime Minister will need to act fast
stories.summary: Andy Burnham is certainly not underselling his ascent to the top of the British government, telling Labour Party members on Friday that his election as the new leader of the party was the biggest political change of the last 40 years. Given the raft of huge political changes the UK has seen in the last four decades, it was a significant claim for the man who will take over as British Prime Minister today. It is a big promise for a leader who will be expected not just to deliver, but to deliver fast. He takes over a Number 10 where many in Westminster now joke a revolving door could replace the legendary black entrance we know so well, such is the frequency with which British prime ministers have changed in recent years.

stories.title: Govt leaders to discuss e-scooter concerns with gardaí
stories.summary: The Taoiseach, Tánaiste, Minister for Justice, Minister of State for Transport and the Garda Commissioner are to meet at Government Buildings this morning to discuss safety concerns around e-scooters. Taoiseach Micheál Martin told the Dáil last week that he was leaning towards banning e-scooters, while Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly had said he would support a ban. A recent report by Children's Health Ireland raised concerns about traumatic brain injuries being sustained by children using e-scooters. E-scooter users must be at least 16 years of age, and devices used on public roads cannot exceed a design speed of 20km/h.
